title: slim-airgap-bootstrapping-with-kernel-mod-helpers-and-crio-compat-shim
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: reduce air-gapped bundle size and improve first-boot experience for on-prem installs across diverse Linux distros by shipping minimal, deterministic kernel-module helpers, a small CRI compatibility shim (auto-detects containerd/crio/cri-o), and a seeded OCI index for faster bootstrap. This PR introduces a new 'slim' airgap bundle layout intended for constrained environments and regulatory sites where image size and deterministic install ordering are critical. The change also adds a Terraform helper module to pre-seed a local registry with OCI index manifests and introduces upgrade/rollback metadata hooks to avoid kernel module drift during in-place upgrades.

What changed (summary): single-line install wrappers for kmod packages, kmod-install-helpers that detect distro/package manager (deb/rpm/apk) and try to apply out-of-tree module stubs when kernel headers are unavailable; a tiny CRI-compat shim binary and systemd unit that normalizes container runtime socket locations; helm chart patch to allow offline-only imagePullSecrets and explicit hostPort mappings used by the installer; terraform/modules/oci-seed module to push OCI index manifests and layer-lists to an airgapped registry; upgrade-preflight and rollback-postflight hooks that validate loaded kernel modules and reconcile the sealed vendor-lockfile.

Backwards compatibility: this is additive. Existing full bundles are unchanged; the slim bundle is opt-in via a new --bundle-profile=slim flag in installer bootstrap scripts and a new `bundleProfile: slim` value in the airgap bundle manifest. The kmod helpers are no-op when the runtime reports full bundle capabilities.

Testing and validation: unit tests for the kmod helper logic (bash/shim/test harness) and integration tests in perf-canary that validate install on CentOS 7/8, Rocky 8/9, Ubuntu 18.04/20.04/22.04, and RancherOS derivatives. Manual validation performed in an internal airgapped lab: seeded registry, install, upgrade, rollback.

Checklist:
- [x] New slim bundle layout and manifest schema changes (+ docs)
- [x] kmod install helpers and distro detection script (+ tests)
- [x] CRI shim binary (C minimal) and systemd unit (+ tests)
- [x] Terraform OCI seeder module and example usage
- [x] Helm chart opt-in values for offline-only mode
- [x] Upgrade/rollback hooks and migration test cases
- [x] Release notes and migration guidance

Commits: commit 1: add slim bundle manifest schema and generator templates; commit 2: add kmod helper scripts and unit tests; commit 3: add CRI shim and packaging; commit 4: terraform module for oci-seed and example; commit 5: helm chart values and install templates; commit 6: upgrade/rollback hooks and tests; commit 7: docs and release notes.

Files changed (high level): list below highlights modified paths and representative snippets where helpful. Most files are small scripts, module glue code, or helm value files.

Risks and mitigations: the kmod helpers attempt to operatively load or place out-of-tree module stubs; on systems where kernel headers are available the helpers defer to distro packaging. We run conservative heuristics and fail-safe markers so the installer can fall back to full bundle behaviour. The CRI shim only normalizes socket locations and will exit with a clear error if it cannot proxy; we include clear logs and healthchecks used by the console.

Operator notes: to build a slim bundle run `make airgap-profile BUNDLE_PROFILE=slim` in the private-installer directory. The terraform module `terraform/modules/oci-seed` contains a --dry-run flag to generate index manifests without pushing images for validation.

Migration notes: customers using existing on-prem bundles are unaffected. If teams adopt slim bundles they should run preflight checks included in the repo to ensure kernel module compatibility prior to production rollout.

review_comments: Daniel Kim: Can we narrow the distro detection heuristics to avoid false positives on custom kernels? Suggest adding /lib/modules/<ver>/build check.
Maya Thompson (author): Added build-dir check and fallback path in kmod-helper.sh. Also added a verbose flag for debugging.
Priya Shah: Terraform module needs idempotency checks for stale manifests in the local registry; what happens on partial push?
Maya Thompson (author): oci-seed now writes a .seeded marker with manifest hash and supports --force to re-seed; documented behavior in README.
Anders Müller: CI failed once on Alpine test due to musl edge-case in cri-shim; is this accounted for?
Maya Thompson (author): cri-shim rebuilt with musl-friendly flags and small test harness added; reran CI and green.
release_notes: Added slim airgap bundle profile with kernel module helpers and a CRI compatibility shim; terraform oci-seed module for local registry seeding; helm chart opts for offline-only install. Guidance for adopting slim bundles included.
